themes.label: Hormuz Crisis → Oil Spike → Stagflation Impulse
themes.stance: US strikes on Iran in day nine; tankers crippled in the strait; WTI at ~$79 (+15% in a week) from the prior ~$70 floor. The prior 'Iran deal → disinflation' tell has tripped — the snapback is live. The full $100+ / confirmed-closure scenario is still a tail, not base case, but the pre-emptive flip to long energy, gold, TIPS is justified. Offside: short-oil, long-duration, long-discretionary. Pump pass-through (gas ~$3.86, still below May's ~$4.50) is prospective — energy tax on the consumer not yet in the data.
themes.tell: WTI clearing $100 on a confirmed Hormuz closure is the full stagflation trade. De-escalation back below $70 revives the disinflation book. Aug 12 July CPI ≥+0.4% MoM confirms energy pass-through has flipped inflation back up.

themes.label: Core Inflation Trajectory — Benign or Re-Accelerating
themes.stance: June CPI headline -0.42% MoM (oil-driven) and core -0.02% — the disinflation peak, not a trend. Core PCE still +0.32% MoM in May (~3.9% annualized). The PCE/CPI divergence now resolves hawkish once the crude spike passes through in the July print. TIPS hedge validated; underweight nominal long duration. Aug 12 July CPI is the decisive adjudicator.
themes.tell: Aug 12 July CPI headline ≥+0.4% MoM confirms oil shock has re-accelerated inflation — stay short duration, long TIPS. A soft print despite the crude spike would rebut re-acceleration. Jul 30 June PCE confirms whether core sticks at ~3.9% annualized pre-shock.

themes.label: Fed Boxed In — Stagflation-Lite Policy Trap
themes.stance: Labor softening (payrolls +57k, continuing claims ~1.81M grinding higher) argued for cuts, but the oil/Hormuz shock strips the Fed of cover. 2Y at 4.16 (~53bp above 3.63 funds) — the tape is skeptical of cuts, now correctly so for a new reason. Bull-steepener bias survives only on the front end if labor deteriorates faster than oil lifts inflation. 10Y at 4.57; 10Y–2Y at +0.37 to +0.42. Long-end capped by inflation premium + supply. Jul 28–29 FOMC tone is the near-term gate.
themes.tell: Jul 28–29 FOMC: any hint the Fed cuts through the oil spike is a dovish shock (gold/steepener); a hawkish hold confirms the boxed-in read and pressures multiples. 2Y breaking below 3.63 funds signals recession-fear pricing; holding above 3.90 confirms cut skepticism. Sep 30 funding deadline adds supply pressure.

themes.label: Labor Market Softening → Cut Path Constrained
themes.stance: Direction of labor cooling is confirmed: payrolls +57k, unemployment 4.2% via labor-force exit, continuing claims grinding to 1.81M (up from ~1.78M in May). But the oil shock now overrides the cut logic — the Fed cannot cut cleanly through an energy-led inflation spike. Front-end duration add is conditional: only if labor cracks faster than oil lifts inflation. Aug 7 July payrolls is the next gate — does cooling accelerate into the oil shock (stagflation) or stabilize?
themes.tell: Aug 7 July payrolls: acceleration in job losses alongside the oil shock hardens the stagflation narrative. 2Y staying above 3.90 post-FOMC confirms the market is not pricing a cut-through-inflation scenario. BDC discounts to NAV / credit spread widening remains the first-sign private-credit stress signal.

themes.label: Asset Euphoria vs. Collapsing Consumer Confidence
themes.stance: Gap resolving bearish prospectively: June real retail was +0.6% real (rear-view solid, aided by the CPI drop), but that predates the crude spike. Michigan at a series-low 44.8; home prices softening (Case-Shiller -0.4% from Feb peak through Apr); pump pass-through still coming. The crude spike is the catalyst that closes the gap bearishly — an energy tax on an already-confidence-depleted consumer. Homebuilder and discretionary underweight confirmed.
themes.tell: Aug 15 July retail sales: a negative real print confirms bearish gap resolution and validates discretionary/homebuilder underweight. Gas at the pump sustainably above $4.25/gal (crude pass-through) would accelerate the squeeze. Michigan below 44 is the confidence-collapse confirmation.

themes.label: AI Capex & Moat Risk — Mega-Cap Valuation Overhang
themes.stance: Chinese AI (Kimi K3) is a fresh DeepSeek-style moat scare landing directly into upcoming megacap capex guidance season — reinforces underweight QQQ. High-multiple cohort faces a dual headwind: geopolitical risk-off from Hormuz + moat-compression narrative. Sustained hyperscaler capex (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN late-July earnings) is a dip to buy; margin/capex cuts extend the reset. NVIDIA mid-Aug is the AI demand-confirmation gate.
themes.tell: Late-Jul/Early-Aug MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN capex guidance sustained or raised = AI dip to buy. Capex cuts or gross-margin warnings = multiple reset, stay underweight QQQ. NVIDIA Q2 FY27 (mid-Aug) is the AI demand-confirmation gate. Kimi K3 pricing undercuts US model pricing = moat erosion accelerating.

themes.label: Secular Defense Rearmament Bid
themes.stance: Doubly reinforced: Russia's largest ballistic-missile barrage on Kyiv yet, NATO warnings on the Baltics, and now a hot US–Iran war in its ninth day. Two simultaneous hot wars eliminate any near-term peace-dividend risk. XAR overweight maintained. Rare-earth/input-cost margin risk for defense primes remains the key watch.
themes.tell: NATO/EU defense budget commitments rising above 2.5% GDP targets confirm secular bid. Defense prime earnings guidance cuts citing rare-earth or labor cost pressure introduce margin risk. A comprehensive Ukraine or Iran ceasefire is the structural refutation — currently off the table.

themes.label: Divided Government → Fiscal Gridlock & Supply Risk
themes.stance: Gridlock structurally intact; markets pricing D House (84.5%) / R Senate (56.5%) post-midterms = persistent gridlock, no demand-side fiscal stimulus, deficit-driven supply story into FY27. Sep 30 government funding deadline is the near-term crystallization event. Long-end supply risk compounded by the inflation premium from the oil shock — 10Y capped on both the supply and inflation side.
themes.tell: Sep 30 government funding deadline: shutdown or last-minute CR confirms gridlock. Nov 3 midterm D House result resolves split government as base case. 10Y >4.75% on Treasury auction indigestion confirms long-end supply risk is live.
